text:
Marathon Petroleum fell slightly today, giving back a fraction of the strong gains it posted over the past two weeks. The decline came despite oil prices rising again on Monday—U.S. crude moved up to $101.91 a barrel—after Houthi militants claimed attacks on Saudi Arabian airports and energy facilities. The stock's weakness appears to reflect profit-taking after a 9% run-up since early October, rather than any deterioration in the refining environment itself.

Refineries are running at a healthy 93.5%, and geopolitical turmoil in the Middle East continues to support crude prices, which is generally good for refiner margins. However, the modest pullback suggests investors may be consolidating after the recent rally that tracked rising oil prices and escalating regional tensions over the past week.
